A PDF isn’t a plain‑text file, so you can’t “sort it by line” in the usual way.

|------|--------------|-------------|
| 1️⃣ Convert the PDF → TXT | Turns the visual layout into raw text lines. | ```bash\npdftotext final_report.pdf report_text.txt\n``` |

| 3️⃣ Sort the lines | Alphabetical order gives a quick view of everything. | ```bash\nsort report_text.txt > report_sorted.txt\n``` |
| 4️⃣ Re‑package (optional) | Turn the sorted text back into a nicely formatted PDF. | ```bash\npandoc report_sorted.txt -o final_report_sorted.pdf\n``` |

Below is a step‑by‑step recipe you can drop straight into a Linux/Unix/Mac terminal (or adapt it for PowerShell / CMD).  
It moves one more PDF into the `temp` folder, extracts the text from each PDF, and runs a side‑by‑side comparison so you can spot every substantive change between the old (“previous”) version and the new (“final”) report.

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> • A recent installation of **Poppler** (`pdftotext`)  
> • **Pandoc** (for optional pretty printing)  
> • Standard GNU utilities (`diff`, `sed`, `awk`, …)

--------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1️⃣ Put everything together in `temp`

```bash
cd ~/your_project/document           # ← adjust to wherever your repo lives
mkdir -p temp                        # make sure the folder exists

# Move the extra file you asked for:
mv previous_report.pdf temp/
# (Now temp holds: final_report.pdf + previous_report.pdf)
```

> If you wanted to bring in `report_final.pdf` instead, replace the filename above.

--------------------------------------------------------------------

## 2️⃣ Pull the raw text out of each PDF

Create a temporary workspace so we don’t clutter the main tree:

```bash
mkdir -p tmp_txt && pushd tmp_txt >/dev/null   # enter tmp_txt
```

Extract the two PDFs:

```bash
pdftotext ../temp/final_report.pdf  final.txt
pdftotext ../temp/previous_report.pdf prev.txt
```

The result:  
• `final.txt` – unformatted, line‑based dump of the final report  
• `prev.txt`  – same for the previous report

--------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3️⃣ Clean up a little (optional)

Sometimes PDFs include page numbers, headers, footers… that bloat diffs.  
Here’s a tiny helper that strips common artifacts:

```bash
# Strip empty lines and leading/trailing whitespace
sed -i '/^$/d;s/^ *//g;s/ *$//' *.txt
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------

## 4️⃣ Run the actual comparison

```bash
diff --unified=5 prev.txt final.txt > report_diff.patch
less report_diff.patch      # scroll through the patch
```

Or, if you prefer a colorized, side‑by‑side view:

```bash
colordiff -y prev.txt final.txt | less -R
```

Every block marked with `<` comes from the *old* report, while blocks marked with `>` come from the *new* one.  
Look especially for:

* New headings or removed sections  
* Substantial numeric shifts (budgets, forecasts, KPIs)  
* Added or deleted tables/charts (they appear as long strings of table delimiters)

--------------------------------------------------------------------

## 5️⃣ Highlight the “critical” differences

To surface only the most important changes (say, anything touching the word **budget**, **forecast**, **revenue**, etc.):

```bash
grep -E "(budget|forecast|revenue)" report_diff.patch
```

That prints only those hunks that reference key business terms.

--------------------------------------------------------------------

## 6️⃣ Wrap‑up: put everything cleanly back

```bash
popd >/dev/null    # leave tmp_txt
rm -rf tmp_txt     # delete the scratch space
```

Your `temp` folder now looks like:

```
temp/
├─ final_report.pdf
└─ previous_report.pdf
```

…and you’ve got a ready‑to‑review `report_diff.patch` showing exactly what changed.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### TL;DR Commands

```bash
cd ~/project/document
mkdir -p temp
mv previous_report.pdf temp/
mkdir -p tmp_txt && pushd tmp_txt
pdftotext ../temp/final_report.pdf  final.txt
pdftotext ../temp/previous_report.pdf prev.txt
sed -i '/^$/d;s/^ *//g;s/ *$//' *.txt
diff --unified=5 prev.txt final.txt > report_diff.patch
less report_diff.patch
popd && rm -rf tmp_txt
```

Run those, open `report_diff.patch`, and you’ll instantly see every headline, figure, or paragraph that differs between the two versions. Happy reviewing!
